slot.subtopic: Field of a dipole on equatorial line
slot.brief: Given dipole moment, find the electric field magnitude at a point on the equatorial line at a given distance.

stem: An ideal electric dipole has moment $6.0\times10^{-8}$ C m. The magnitude of the electric field at a point $0.30$ m from its centre on the equatorial line is, in air. Take $k=9.0\times10^9$ N m$^2$ C$^{-2}$, as shown in the figure.

verdicts.working: On the equatorial line, the dipole field magnitude is E = kp/r^3 = (9.0×10^9)(6.0×10^-8)/(0.30)^3 = 2.0×10^4 N C^-1.

working:
$E=\dfrac{kp}{r^3}=\dfrac{(9.0\times10^9)(6.0\times10^{-8})}{(0.30)^3}=2.0\times10^4\ \text{N C}^{-1}$

solution:
On the equatorial line, the dipole field magnitude is $E=\dfrac{kp}{r^3}$.
$$E=\frac{(9.0\times10^9)(6.0\times10^{-8})}{(0.30)^3}=2.0\times10^4\ \text{N C}^{-1}$$
